::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Compactness of three dimensional torus](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2521606/compactness-of-three-dimensional-torus), asked by [AlphaXY](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/482385/alphaxy) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-11-15; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> The three dimensional torus  (the periodic domain in Navier-Stokes equations $\mathbb{T}^3=(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^3$) is compact.  Can anyone here give us a detailed proof.
:::

It's a quotient space of $[0,1]^3$, or homeomorphic to $S^1 \times S^1 \times S^1$.
